name: China-Solomon Islands security pact and policing deal
value: Security agreement signed April 2022 (text not published; a leaked draft allows Chinese police, armed police and military deployments); policing cooperation pact July 2023; Chinese police trainers, equipment and vehicles
lender_builder: Chinese government / Ministry of Public Security
china_gets: A legal basis for Chinese security forces and ship visits in the South Pacific
host_position: Honiara says there will be no Chinese base and that the deal fills security gaps; Australia, the US and New Zealand object
confidence_reason: Signing is confirmed, but the final text is secret; its scope rests on a leaked draft

name: Honiara national stadium (2023 Pacific Games)
value: About $50m, built and paid for by China
china_gets: A showcase project after the 2019 switch of diplomatic recognition from Taiwan
host_position: The government welcomed it as the Games venue
confidence_reason: Cost reported by the Washington Post only

name: Huawei mobile towers (161 sites)
value: $66m China Exim loan (2022) for 161 towers built by Huawei; the country's first loan from China
china_gets: A national telecom footprint for Huawei
host_position: The government called it a historic financing partnership; Australia had earlier funded the Coral Sea cable to keep Huawei out
confidence_reason: Loan reported by the Guardian and the Georgetown Journal of International Affairs (GJIA)

name: Ramu NiCo nickel-cobalt mine and Basamuk refinery
value: About $2bn project; MCC-led company holds 85%; slurry spill at Basamuk in 2019 (about 200,000 litres, 80,000 reached the sea)
lender_builder: Metallurgical Corporation of China (MCC) with Jinchuan, Jiuquan and Jilin Jien
china_gets: Nickel and cobalt supply for batteries
host_position: PNG briefly shut the plant after the spill, then let it reopen; local communities remain concerned
confidence_reason: Ownership from the NI 43-101 technical report; spill reported by ABC and The National

name: Kumul domestic submarine cable
value: $229m China Exim buyer's credit for 85% of a $270m Huawei contract; about 5,500km of cable completed 2020; repayment terms amended in 2021
china_gets: Huawei-built core of PNG's domestic internet backbone
host_position: PNG DataCo struggled to repay; the cable's viability was questioned

name: Luganville main wharf
value: RMB541.9m (about $87m) China Exim concessional loan (2014; 2%, 20 years); 361m wharf handed over in 2017
china_gets: A deep-water wharf in the South Pacific; 2018 media reports of base talks were denied
host_position: Vanuatu says it is a civilian cargo and cruise wharf
confidence_reason: Loan terms in AidData; base reports are denied and not used as evidence

name: Tanna and Malekula roads
value: RMB350m China Exim loan (2014; 2%, 20 years) for 45km of roads, finished 2019; a second RMB350m loan for phase 2
china_gets: Construction contracts; China is Vanuatu's largest bilateral creditor
host_position: Vanuatu says the roads improve island access

name: Tonga's China Exim debt (Nuku'alofa rebuild)
value: China Exim held 47% of Tonga's external debt in mid-2024 (54% in 2023); repayments peaked at about 3% of GDP in FY2024; TOP$42m due in FY2025 (61% of debt service)
lender_builder: China Exim (loans for rebuilding the centre of Nuku'alofa after the 2006 riots)
host_position: Tonga had repayments deferred under the G20 debt suspension scheme (DSSI) and now avoids new non-concessional borrowing
confidence_reason: From the IMF debt sustainability analysis and Tonga's Ministry of Finance

name: Vaiusu Bay wharf (cancelled)
value: Proposed $100m China-backed wharf (earlier $300m and judged unviable by the ADB); cancelled in 2021; China already held about 40% of Samoa's external debt
host_position: New Prime Minister Fiame cancelled it as excessive debt exposure
confidence_reason: Cancellation confirmed; the project never got past feasibility work

name: Kanton Island airstrip upgrade
value: No figures; China said in 2021 it was studying the feasibility of an upgrade at Kiribati's invitation
china_gets: A possible mid-Pacific runway about 3,000km from Hawaii
host_position: Kiribati says the project is civilian (transport and tourism)
confidence_reason: Only feasibility work is confirmed, with no contract or financing; the strategic concerns are speculative

name: Cook Islands-China partnership (seabed minerals, infrastructure)
value: Five-year action plan signed in February 2025 covering seabed-mineral research, infrastructure, ports and shipping; no figures; no mining licences
china_gets: Access to research on one of the world's largest nodule fields
host_position: The Cook Islands says it protects its interests; New Zealand objected to not being consulted and paused funding
confidence_reason: The agreement is signed and public, but no projects have been delivered yet

name: Fiji-China police cooperation agreement
value: 2011 memorandum kept after a 2024 review, but Chinese officers embedded in Fiji's police were sent home; Fijian officers still train in China
china_gets: A policing foothold in a key Pacific state
host_position: Rabuka's government narrowed it but did not cancel it
confidence_reason: The review outcome was reported by the Guardian, ABC and FBC
